The guy is not wrong. The 25/3 standard creates a disincentive to deploy if you can't reach that level. In rural areas, 25 to each end-point is pretty ambitious and most cities don't do better than 10-15 on coax/copper. By lowering the fixed wired classification to a more reachable goal of 10/1 you end up with more people with a quality connection. 10/1 is a perfectly good internet connection - it won't stream 4k video but it will do pretty much everything else you need on the web. Finally, it's smarter to push standards in high-bandwidth mobile for future demands. The model being proposed here stands a better chance of achieving the actual goal in real life: A basic and decent fixed wired internet connection for as many people as possible plus a robust mobile option.
